annotation.title_clean: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.title_en: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department of Law, Shanxi University of Finance and Economics
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Chinese legal article typifying tort liability for humanoid robots into passive and active infringement, focusing on learning-algorithm harms. Using law and economics (Hand Formula), it allocates liability among manufacturers, general AI model providers (joint liability if transparency fails) and users, treating ordinary defects under product liability.
key_provisions_or_claims: Infringement divided into passive (user/third-party caused) and independent (hardware, ordinary algorithm, learning algorithm) types.
Hardware and ordinary software defects handled under product liability, with defect presumption via information disclosure.
Manufacturers' duty calibrated by the Hand Formula and by technology stage and application risk level.
General AI model providers jointly liable with robot makers if they fail transparency obligations.
Users bear liability for negligence or malicious teaching; propose a robot 'black box' recorder and third-party audits.
